I met same issue. 
$ curl  http://x.x.x.x:2379
404 page not found

But I met this error log:
embed: ready to serve client requests
embed: serving insecure client requests on 127.0.0.1:2379, this is strongly discouraged!
embed: serving insecure client requests on 192.168.122.72:2379, this is strongly discouraged!

@philips, thanks for response. curl http://x.x.x.x:2379 got 404 page not found error.

c910f04x35k10:~ # curl http://10.4.35.10:2379
404 page not found
c910f04x35k10:~ # curl http://10.4.35.11:2379
404 page not found
c910f04x35k10:~ # curl http://10.4.35.12:2379
404 page not found
c910f04x35k10:~ #

BTW, I setup Kubernetes using this etcd cluster, seems Kubernetes is working correctly...

I tried fetching the v2 health endpoint on a fresh cluster that I know works:
```sh
 $ curl http://localhost:2379/health
{"health": "false"}
```

Looks like cluster-health is broken and there's no e2e test to catch it.
@heyitsanthony hm... it probably breaks on master but not the version he used. I remember v2 cluster-health actually depends on the periodic `Sync` request.

issue.title: v2http: submit QGET in health endpoint if no progress

repository.name: etcd
repository.description: Distributed reliable key-value store for the most critical data of a distributed system

issue.body:
Removing the periodic SYNC calls broke the health endpoint since the
raft index stops updating. Instead, if there is no activity after 250ms, issue
a QGET to force some raft traffic.
    
Fixes #6985

issue.title: why change the code for dealing with ‘/health’ interface in v3 version?
